newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-COETZER FACES UNKNOWN PROSPECT IN QUARTER-FINALS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-COETZER FACES UNKNOWN PROSPECT IN QUARTER-FINALS.

text.p: South Africa's Amanda Coetzer, fresh from her upset victory over top seed Steffi Graf, faces an unknown quantity in American Kimberly Po in the quarter-finals of the Australian Open on Tuesday.
Po, world ranked 23, has nothing to lose having already posted career-best grand slam results at Melbourne Park this year, but has never played Coetzer in nearly a decade of professional tennis.

The 25-year-old from California has never advanced beyond the third round in 18 previous grand slams. She has performed way beyond expectations here, upsetting her seventh seeded compatriot Lindsay Davenport in the fourth round.
Coetzer, the 12th seed, played the match of her life to beat Graf in the fourth round on baking a Centre Court on Sunday.
The diminutive South African handled the boiling conditions perfectly, waiting patiently on the baseline for Graf to make a mistake.
Heatwave conditions have been forecast to continue in Melbourne on Tuesday with the temperature tipped to break the 40-degree Celsius mark for the third day running.

In the other women's quarter-final, 1995 champion Mary Pierce will be looking to continue her winning streak against seeded players, having already disposed of fifth seed Anke Huber and 13th seed Elena Likhovtseva.
The French player takes on 16th seed Sabine Appelmans in the a night match.
Pierce has dropped only 11 games in her past three matches and the aggressive, athletic game which helped her win two years ago seems to have returned.
Both men's quarter-finals promise marathon baseline duels with American second seed Michael Chang aiming to register his fourth straight career victory over Chile's Marcelo Rios, the ninth seed.
In an all-Spanish affair, 14th seed Felix Mantilla and giant killer Carlos Moya meet in the other men's match.
Moya caused the biggest upset in the men's draw when he beat defending champion Boris Becker in the first round.
